title: Ginisang patola
intro: Sponge gourd sautéed with shrimp, garlic and tomatoes until soft and swimming in its own sweet juices. Light and mild, best with rice and something fried on the side.

steps.text: Scrape off the hard ridges of the patola with a peeler, leaving strips of green skin. Slice diagonally into 1 cm pieces.
Heat the oil in a pan over medium heat. Cook the garlic, onion and tomatoes until the tomatoes soften.
Add the shrimp and cook until they just turn pink. Season with the fish sauce.
Add the patola and water, cover and simmer until the patola is tender and translucent.
Season with pepper, taste for salt, sprinkle with green onions and serve.

tips: Taste a slice of raw patola before cooking; very occasionally one is bitter, and that one should go.

title: Ginisang okra
intro: Sliced okra sautéed with lots of tomato and onion, then bound with a little scrambled egg. The tomato cuts the sliminess, and the result is soft, tangy and savory.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a wide pan over medium-high heat. Add the okra in a single layer and let it sear without stirring, then toss and sear the other side.
Add the garlic and onion and cook until soft.
Add the tomatoes and soy sauce and cook until the tomatoes break down and the okra is tender.
Pour the eggs over, let them set for a few seconds, then fold gently until just cooked.
Season with salt and pepper and serve with rice.

tips: Dry the okra well after washing and sear it in a hot pan before adding anything wet; that keeps it from turning slimy.

title: Ginisang Baguio beans
intro: Green beans and carrot sautéed with browned ground pork in a savory oyster and soy sauce glaze. Crisp, salty-sweet and quick enough for a weeknight.

items.name: Baguio beans (green beans)
items.note: trimmed and cut diagonally into 4 cm pieces

steps.text: Heat the oil in a pan over medium-high heat and cook the pork, breaking it up, until browned.
Add the garlic and onion and cook until soft.
Add the beans, carrot, oyster sauce, soy sauce and water. Toss, cover and cook until the beans are tender-crisp.
Uncover and toss until the sauce coats the vegetables. Season with pepper and serve.

tips: For the brightest color, stop cooking while the beans still squeak a little when you bite one.

title: Ginisang sigarilyas
intro: Winged beans sliced into little stars and sautéed with pork belly, garlic and tomatoes. They stay crunchy and taste like a cross between green beans and asparagus.

steps.text: Put the pork in a dry pan over medium heat and cook until it renders its fat and turns golden.
Add the garlic, onion and tomatoes and cook until soft. Season with the fish sauce.
Add the sigarilyas and water and toss. Cover and cook until tender-crisp.
Uncover, season with pepper, taste for salt and serve.

tips: Pick young, bright green pods that snap cleanly. Older pods are fibrous and need a few more minutes.

title: Ginisang kalabasa at sitaw
intro: Cubes of squash and long beans sautéed with shrimp and simmered until the squash is soft enough to thicken the sauce. Sweet, savory and very good with fried fish.

items.name: kalabasa (squash)
items.note: peeled and cut into 2 cm cubes

steps.text: Heat the oil in a pot over medium heat. Cook the garlic, onion and tomato until soft.
Add the shrimp and cook until pink. Lift them out and set aside so they do not overcook.
Add the squash, fish sauce and water. Cover and simmer until the squash is almost tender.
Add the sitaw, cover and cook until tender and the squash starts to soften at the edges.
Return the shrimp, stir gently, season with pepper and taste for salt before serving.

tips: Kabocha-type squash with dark green skin holds its shape better than the pale, watery kinds.

title: Chopsuey
intro: A colorful stir-fry of mixed vegetables with chicken, shrimp and quail eggs in a glossy oyster sauce gravy. The vegetables stay crisp and the sauce is savory and lightly sweet.

steps.text: Have every vegetable cut and ready before you start; the cooking goes fast.
Heat the oil in a wok over medium-high heat. Cook the garlic and onion until soft.
Add the chicken and stir-fry until it turns white and is cooked through.
Add the shrimp and cook until pink.
Stir in the oyster sauce, soy sauce and water and bring to a boil. Add the carrot and cauliflower, cover and cook.
Add the broccoli, snow peas and bell pepper, cover and cook.
Add the cabbage and quail eggs and toss until the cabbage just wilts.
Stir the cornstarch mixture, pour it in and toss until the sauce turns glossy and thickens. Season with salt and pepper and serve right away.

tips: Cook in order of firmness, hardest vegetables first, so nothing turns soft. Pork or sliced pork liver can stand in for the chicken.

title: Vegetarian chopsuey
intro: Chopsuey made with fried tofu and mushrooms in a light soy and garlic gravy instead of meat and oyster sauce. Crunchy, savory and colorful.

items.name: firm tofu
items.note: patted dry and cut into 2 cm cubes

steps.text: Heat the oil in a wok over medium-high heat and fry the tofu until golden on most sides. Lift out and set aside.
In the oil left in the wok, cook the mushrooms until they brown and their liquid evaporates.
Add the garlic and onion and cook until soft.
Stir in the soy sauce, sugar and vegetable broth and bring to a boil. Add the carrot and cauliflower, cover and cook.
Add the broccoli, snow peas and bell pepper, cover and cook.
Add the cabbage and tofu and toss until the cabbage just wilts.
Stir the cornstarch mixture, pour it in and toss until glossy. Drizzle with sesame oil, season and serve.

tips: Brown the mushrooms well; they give the gravy the savory depth that meat and oyster sauce would.

title: Ginisang monggo with pork
intro: Mung beans boiled until creamy, then simmered with sautéed pork belly, garlic and tomatoes and finished with spinach. Thick, savory and hearty, poured over rice.

items.name: dried mung beans (monggo)
items.note: about 200 g, rinsed and picked over

steps.text: Put the mung beans and water in a pot and bring to a boil. Lower the heat, partly cover and simmer until the beans are soft and many have split open.
Meanwhile, put the pork in a dry pan over medium heat and cook until it renders its fat and turns golden.
Add the garlic and onion to the pork and cook until soft, then add the tomatoes and cook until they break down.
Scrape the pork mixture into the beans and season with the fish sauce. Simmer, stirring now and then so it does not catch, until thick and creamy. Add hot water if it gets too thick.
Stir in the spinach and cook until wilted. Season with salt and pepper and serve with rice.

tips: Monggo thickens a lot as it stands. Loosen leftovers with hot water when reheating.

title: Ginisang monggo with tinapa
intro: Creamy mung bean stew flavored with flaked smoked fish instead of meat. The tinapa gives it a smoky, salty depth, and it is a favorite on meatless days.

items.name: dried mung beans (monggo)
items.note: about 200 g, rinsed and picked over

items.name: tinapa (smoked fish)
items.note: about 200 g, skin and bones removed, flaked

steps.text: Put the mung beans and water in a pot and bring to a boil. Lower the heat, partly cover and simmer until soft and split.
Meanwhile, heat the oil in a pan over medium heat. Cook the garlic and onion until soft, then the tomatoes until they break down.
Add the flaked tinapa and fry, stirring, until fragrant.
Scrape the tinapa mixture into the beans and season with the fish sauce. Simmer, stirring now and then, until thick and creamy.
Stir in the greens and cook until wilted. Taste before adding salt, since tinapa is already salty. Serve with rice.

tips: Take your time removing the bones from the tinapa; the small ones are easy to miss once they are in the stew.

title: Monggo with malunggay and chicharon
intro: Mung bean stew loaded with malunggay leaves and topped with crushed pork chicharon just before serving. The chicharon softens at the edges and adds salty, porky crunch.

items.name: dried mung beans (monggo)
items.note: about 200 g, rinsed and picked over

steps.text: Put the mung beans and water in a pot and bring to a boil. Lower the heat, partly cover and simmer until soft and split.
Meanwhile, heat the oil in a pan over medium heat. Cook the garlic and onion until soft, then the tomatoes until they break down.
Scrape the sauté into the beans and season with the fish sauce. Simmer, stirring now and then, until thick and creamy.
Stir in the malunggay and cook until just wilted. Season with salt and pepper.
Ladle into bowls and top each with chicharon at the table so it stays crunchy.

tips: Taste the stew before adding the chicharon; it brings a lot of salt, so season the monggo lightly.

title: Ginisang monggo with tofu
intro: A meatless monggo with cubes of fried tofu and squash, seasoned with soy sauce and salt. Thick, creamy and filling, with sweetness from the squash.

items.name: dried mung beans (monggo)
items.note: about 200 g, rinsed and picked over

items.name: firm tofu
items.note: patted dry and cut into 2 cm cubes

steps.text: Put the mung beans and water in a pot and bring to a boil. Lower the heat, partly cover and simmer until soft and split.
Meanwhile, heat the oil in a pan over medium-high heat and fry the tofu until golden. Lift out and set aside.
In the same oil, cook the garlic and onion until soft, then the tomatoes until they break down.
Add the sauté, squash and soy sauce to the beans. Simmer, stirring now and then, until the squash is tender and the stew is thick.
Stir in the tofu and heat through. Season well with salt and pepper and serve.

tips: Without fish sauce or meat, monggo needs more salt than you expect. Season, wait a minute, and taste again.

title: Ginisang monggo with ampalaya leaves
intro: Mung bean stew with shrimp and a big handful of bitter gourd leaves stirred in at the end. The leaves add a gentle bitterness that the creamy beans soften.

items.name: dried mung beans (monggo)
items.note: about 200 g, rinsed and picked over

steps.text: Put the mung beans and water in a pot and bring to a boil. Lower the heat, partly cover and simmer until soft and split.
Meanwhile, heat the oil in a pan over medium heat. Cook the garlic and onion until soft, then the tomatoes until they break down.
Add the shrimp to the pan and cook just until pink.
Scrape the shrimp mixture into the beans and season with the fish sauce. Simmer until thick and creamy.
Stir in the ampalaya leaves and cook just until wilted. Season with salt and pepper and serve.

tips: Add the leaves at the very end and turn off the heat; the longer they cook, the more bitter the whole pot becomes.

title: Tokwa with oyster sauce
intro: Golden fried tofu cubes tossed in a glossy oyster sauce gravy with garlic and green onions. Crisp outside, soft inside and very good over hot rice.

items.name: firm tofu
items.note: 2 blocks, patted dry and cut into 3 cm cubes

steps.text: Heat the oil in a wide pan over medium-high heat. Fry the tofu in batches, turning, until golden and crisp on all sides. Drain on paper towels.
Pour off all but 1 tablespoon of oil. Cook the garlic and onion over medium heat until soft.
Add the oyster sauce, soy sauce, sugar and water and bring to a simmer.
Stir the cornstarch mixture and pour it in, stirring until the sauce thickens.
Add the tofu and green onions and toss gently to coat. Serve right away while the tofu is still crisp.

tips: Press the tofu between paper towels under a plate for 15 minutes before cutting; drier tofu fries crisper and spatters less.

title: Tofu with sweet chili sauce
intro: Cornstarch-coated tofu fried until crunchy and tossed in a quick sweet chili, garlic and calamansi glaze. Sticky, sweet, a little spicy and gone fast.

items.name: firm tofu
items.note: 2 blocks, pressed and cut into 3 cm cubes

steps.text: Toss the tofu with the cornstarch and salt until every piece is coated.
Heat the oil in a wide pan over medium-high heat. Fry the tofu in batches, turning, until crisp and golden. Drain on a rack.
Pour off all but 1 tablespoon of oil. Fry the garlic over medium heat until fragrant.
Add the sweet chili sauce, soy sauce and calamansi juice and let it bubble until slightly thickened.
Add the tofu and toss to coat. Scatter with green onions and sesame seeds and serve immediately.

tips: Toss the tofu in the sauce only at the last minute; the coating softens the longer it sits.

title: Tofu bistek
intro: Slabs of fried tofu simmered briefly in a salty-sour sauce of soy sauce and calamansi, topped with soft onion rings. All the flavor of bistek Tagalog without the beef.

items.name: firm tofu
items.note: 2 blocks, pressed and sliced 1.5 cm thick

steps.text: Heat the oil in a wide pan over medium-high heat. Fry the tofu slices until golden on both sides. Drain on paper towels.
In the same oil, cook the onion rings over medium heat until just soft but not browned. Lift out half for topping.
Add the garlic and cook until fragrant. Pour in the soy sauce, calamansi juice, sugar, water and pepper and bring to a simmer.
Lay the tofu in the sauce and simmer, turning once, until the sauce reduces slightly and the tofu soaks some up.
Top with the reserved onion rings and serve with rice.

tips: Taste the sauce before adding the tofu; it should be salty and sour with a hint of sweet. Add calamansi or water to balance.

title: Tokwa with tausi
intro: Fried tofu and bell pepper in a thick sauce of salted black beans, garlic and ginger. Salty, savory and a little pungent, so you need plenty of rice with it.

items.name: firm tofu
items.note: 2 blocks, pressed and cut into 3 cm cubes

steps.text: Heat the oil in a wide pan over medium-high heat and fry the tofu in batches until golden on all sides. Drain.
Pour off all but 1 tablespoon of oil. Cook the garlic, ginger and onion over medium heat until fragrant.
Add the tausi and bell pepper and stir-fry until the pepper is bright.
Add the soy sauce, sugar and water and bring to a simmer. Stir in the cornstarch mixture and cook until thickened.
Return the tofu, toss gently to coat, scatter with green onions and serve.

tips: Rinse the tausi before using; straight from the can or jar it can make the dish too salty.

title: Ginisang tokwa at giniling
intro: Fried tofu cubes simmered with ground pork in a light tomato and soy sauce gravy. Saucy, savory and a cheap way to feed a family.

items.name: firm tofu
items.note: pressed and cut into 2 cm cubes

steps.text: Heat the oil in a wide pan over medium-high heat and fry the tofu until golden. Lift out and set aside.
Pour off all but 1 tablespoon of oil. Cook the garlic and onion until soft, then add the pork and cook, breaking it up, until browned.
Add the tomatoes and cook until they soften.
Stir in the soy sauce, oyster sauce and water. Add the tofu and simmer until the sauce thickens slightly.
Season with pepper, scatter with green onions and serve with rice.

tips: A handful of frozen green peas added with the tofu makes it go further.

title: Ginisang talong sa bagoong
intro: Eggplant pan-fried until soft, then tossed in a sauté of bagoong alamang, tomatoes and garlic. Creamy, salty and a little sweet.

items.name: long eggplants
items.note: about 500 g, cut into 5 cm pieces and quartered lengthwise

steps.text: Heat 3 tablespoons of the oil in a wide pan over medium-high heat. Fry the eggplant in batches until golden and soft. Set aside.
Add the rest of the oil and cook the garlic, onion and tomatoes over medium heat until the tomatoes break down.
Stir in the bagoong, sugar and chili and cook until fragrant.
Add the water and the eggplant and toss gently until coated and heated through.
Taste and serve with rice.

tips: Eggplant drinks oil. Fry it in a hot pan in a single layer and do not keep adding oil; it releases some back as it softens.

title: Ginisang chicharo with shrimp
intro: Snow peas and carrot stir-fried with shrimp in a light oyster sauce glaze. Sweet, crunchy and done in about ten minutes.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a wok over medium-high heat. Cook the garlic and onion until soft.
Add the shrimp and stir-fry until just pink.
Add the carrot, snow peas, oyster sauce and water and toss until the snow peas are bright green and tender-crisp.
Stir the cornstarch mixture, add it and toss until the sauce turns glossy. Season with salt and pepper and serve.

tips: Snow peas go from crisp to limp quickly. Pull the pan off the heat as soon as they turn bright green.

title: Ginisang puso ng saging
intro: Thinly sliced banana blossom, salted and squeezed to remove the bitter sap, then sautéed with shrimp, garlic and tomatoes. Tender with a slight crunch, savory and mild.

steps.text: Peel off the tough, dark outer bracts of the banana blossom until you reach the pale inner part. Cut it in half lengthwise and slice thinly crosswise, discarding the hard core.
Toss the slices with the salt and massage with your hands until they wilt and release dark sap.
Squeeze hard, rinse in several changes of water and squeeze again until the water runs clear.
Heat the oil in a pan over medium heat. Cook the garlic, onion and tomatoes until the tomatoes soften.
Add the shrimp and cook until pink. Season with the fish sauce.
Add the banana blossom and water, cover and cook, stirring once, until tender.
Uncover and cook off most of the liquid. Season with pepper, taste for salt and serve.

tips: Wear gloves or oil your hands when slicing banana blossom; the sap stains skin and cutting boards dark.

title: Steamed okra and eggplant with bagoong
intro: Whole okra and eggplant steamed until tender and served with a quick sautéed bagoong and fresh tomatoes for dipping. Simple, salty and fresh, a classic side for fried or grilled fish.

steps.text: Bring water to a boil in a steamer. Lay the eggplant in the basket, cover and steam.
Add the okra and steam until both are tender: the eggplant should be soft all the way through and the okra bright green.
Meanwhile, heat the oil in a small pan over medium heat. Cook the garlic and onion until soft.
Add the bagoong, sugar and vinegar and cook, stirring, until the bagoong darkens slightly and smells toasty.
Arrange the vegetables on a plate with the tomatoes and serve the bagoong on the side for dipping.

tips: No steamer? Set the vegetables on a plate over a rack in a covered pot with 2 cm of boiling water, or lay them on top of the rice in the last 10 minutes of cooking.
